construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Stability amplifying stability — holding force deepening without movement
candidates.k2_overview: Your Earth moves as the Twin: ground that holds its own plot beside everyone else’s. You are the neighbor with the straight fence, generous across it, immovable about where it runs. Belonging matters to you, but merger does not. You stand with people the way hills stand in a range: together, and entirely yourselves.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy is bedrock steady: unhurried, unshakable through long loads, renewed by routine.

k2_domain_readings.Peers: Your peers are landholders like you: solid people with their own ground and no designs on yours. Trade help across fences freely. The neighbors you respect at seventy are the wealth this position promises.
k2_domain_readings.Independence: Earth independence is owned ground: a home, a trade, a name that stands without cosigners. You will have it, because you refuse alternatives. Just leave a gate in the fence.
k2_domain_readings.Self-reliance: You carry your own weather and everyone else’s overflow without filing complaints. Twice a year, let someone shovel your side. The ground stays firmer when it is not also the whole world’s floor.

angles.drive: On your own terms, you set a bar and trust it more than any outside grade. Each time you clear it, you set it a little higher. If you leave it in place for a week, you get the satisfaction you keep putting off.
angles.cost_self: Where you set your own bar, you set it alone. Since no one else's standard moves you, you stay steady while you skip the help a peer would give. Let a peer check the bar sometimes, and you win back the help you walk past.
angles.cost_others: The bar you set for yourself travels to everyone beside you. Because you never say it, you expect a match rather than ask for one. Say the bar out loud once, and you give the people beside you a fair chance to meet it.

angles.drive: You need no backup, and owing no one is how you feel safe. You trust yourself as backup more than anyone you could call. Go without backup only where it counts, because you need your strength for those days.
angles.cost_self: Without backup you never learn what being covered feels like. You give that relief far more than you accept it, since accepting would mean admitting a need. When you let yourself need backup, you get back the rest you have been doing without.
angles.cost_others: Standing without backup keeps the people who would stand behind you at a distance. You would rather owe nothing than let a friend in, and that leaves them nothing to hold. Call on a friend as backup once, to show them they count.

angles.drive: Whatever the week brings, you hold steady. Calm is what you trust, and you hold steady instead of riding every mood around you. Whenever you hold steady by choice, not from habit, you keep some of that calm for yourself.
angles.cost_self: Holding steady for everyone, you hide your worst days. You absorb a bad day instead of naming it, and it settles in your body as tiredness. Tell one friend about a rough week, to take in some of the comfort you give everyone else.
angles.cost_others: Good news or bad, you hold steady and look the same. You would sooner keep a level face than show a peer what you feel. When you let one peer see what moves you, you stop leaving them to guess what matters.

angles.drive: Whatever the problem, you never ask for help. Needing someone feels like weakness, and you work it out alone instead of handing any of it over. You carry each problem alone for longer than it needs.
angles.cost_self: Pride stays whole when you never ask, and so do your problems. You carry what a quick question would have halved, since being seen needing something hurts more than the weight does. You lose sleep over what one question would have settled.
angles.cost_others: By never asking, you take something from those who would have said yes. You would rather show up than need someone, and you only show your friends the half that is fine. You give your friends no share in the weight you carry.

angles.drive: Tired, you shut people out before anything else. Quiet is how you recover, and you shut people out sooner than ask for the quiet you need. You only ever wanted rest, never distance from the people you love.
angles.cost_self: Where you shut people out, you shut out what you were saving yourself for. Your own company works so well that you mistake it for the plan rather than a break. You pay for that peace in closeness, one quiet evening at a time.
angles.cost_others: Needing rest, you shut out everyone, the people closest to you included. You keep to yourself rather than explain yourself, and you hand a friend your distance before your reason. You take your company from those you love for as long as you rest.

angles.drive: You take no advice you have not tested yourself. Catching your own mistakes matters more to you than having a peer point them out. You spend weeks on mistakes a peer would have caught at a glance.
angles.cost_self: With no advice taken, you learn at full price. Whenever you would rather learn a thing yourself than be told, a friend's one sentence becomes your whole season. You end up repeating mistakes a friend had already solved for you.
angles.cost_others: When a friend offers advice, you thank them and go your own way. You keep your own plan ahead of theirs, and the care they put in goes to waste. You leave your friends unsure whether their help is welcome.

edge.lead: Earth runs through your family, your growth and your social life. It is the home that is still there when you get back, the slow change that holds once it comes, and the friends who find you where they left you.
